clinician.final_diagnosis: The patient and his father are diagnosed with type II hereditary ATD.
clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, a 25-year-old male, presented with recurrent headaches and occasional limb numbness. Genetic testing revealed a novel heterozygous missense mutation in the SERPINC1 gene in the patient, which was also confirmed in his father, indicating a hereditary condition related to antithrombin deficiency (ATD). Laboratory tests showed decreased antithrombin III activity with normal antigen levels in both the patient (72.2% activity, 235 mg/L antigen) and his father (75.1% activity, 263.3 mg/L antigen), consistent with Type II hereditary ATD. Brain MRI for the patient showed multiple white matter hyperintensity lesions, and the father's MRI also revealed multiple asymptomatic white matter lesions, including more bilateral deep paraventricular confluent lesions and brain atrophy. No documented thrombotic events were reported for either the patient or his father.

Patient's brain MRI showed multiple white matter hyperintensity lesions in the periventricular deep white matter, frontal and parietal lobes, some perpendicular to lateral ventricles and some confluent, not enhanced on T1-weighted contrast.
